source_text: I think all agents should sign their commits henceforth or we won't be able to use this system on non-claude sessions, nor will it work well for reverting changes that happen in a dispatch pattern

reply_text:
Plan: the hook reads identity that Agency hands every agent, and I install it in all repos now. The Agency side (Codex, Kimi and dispatch info) goes to a Codex seat. Starting with the hook.Hook is installed in all 54 repos. Now sending the Agency side (so Codex and Kimi processes know who they are) to codex-4.Gist: Agreed, and half of it is in place. The signing hook now covers every agent, and it's linked into all 54 repos under `~/code`. codex-4 is building the other half: Agency telling each Codex and Kimi process who it is and which job it's running. Until that lands, only Claude seats actually sign. After it, a commit made by a dispatched agent also names the session that dispatched it. Then I'll extend `R` so rewinding a turn also reverts the commits of work that turn sent out.

**The hook** (futon3c 614f8d29): it now adds up to four lines per commit.
- `Agent-Session`: the committing session.
- `Agent-Id`: the committing agent.
- `Agency-Job`: the job it was running.
- `Dispatched-By`: the agent and session that sent the job.

I tried four committers on a scratch repo:
- a Claude session gets its session line;
- a Kimi with job details gets all four lines;
- a commit with no agent identity (you at a terminal) stays unsigned;
- an agent with no job details gets just its id.

It never blocks a commit.

**What codex-4 is doing** (job `invoke-1790738661109-28120-b0f46b89`, park `park-255c6c51-024b-4c90-9091-2cda2af4c67b`):
- **Identity:** it sets the agent id in the process where each agent runs commands. That's the Claude seat process, Codex's `exec`, and the JVM shell that runs Kimi and Zai commands.
- **Job details:** at the start of every job, it writes a small file with the job id, the caller and the caller's session.
- **Acceptance:** one real Codex job and one real Kimi job each commit to a scratch repo, and both commits must show all the lines. A planted case checks that a second job doesn't carry the first job's id.

**Instructions for agents:** I updated the signing section in the workspace `CLAUDE.md` and added one to `AGENTS.md`, telling agents the lines are added for them and not to touch them.

**Not covered:**
- repos cloned from now on need the hook linked by hand (the command is in `CLAUDE.md`);
- the other machines (lucy, oxf).

**Queue:**
- **Corpus:** codex-5 has finished it; I'll review it when its wake-up arrives.
- **象's backlog:** the job list shows about nine 象 readings queued or running at once. That's a large backlog, probably from futon1b being slow earlier. I haven't looked into it.

The tests pass the check: each of the three planted bugs makes its test fail. Writing the baseline down before the next measurement, as criterion 2 requires, then dispatching.Gist: I've accepted the corpus, and codex-5 has moved on to the next step: inducing one guard-and-result rule and testing it against a baseline I wrote down first. Coverage went up a lot once the evidence store was used. 26 of the 35 go-ahead turns now have a complete before / move / after record, and 7 of the 13 correction turns do. Every turn without one has a stated reason.

**Coverage** (futon3c 35ec7d66):

| Family | Turns | Complete records | Reply after | Commit after | Missing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Go-ahead | 35 | 26 | 24 | 18 | 8 turn not found, 1 session with no frames |
| Correction (`done-is-observed-running`) | 13 | 7 | 7 (discovery said 3) | 3 (discovery said 2) | 3 session with no frames, 2 not found, 1 no earlier frame |

**What I checked:**
- **Files:** the commit touches only its three files.
- **Tests:** I reran them. Each of the three planted cases fails its test when I put the bug back in:
  - drop the whitespace strip on hashes;
  - count the next turn's rows as this turn's;
  - return an empty record in place of a reason.
- **Spot checks:** turn-iNKHir's record (a reply plus one futon2 commit) and turn-g9JGYE's (a reply, no commits) match their stepper frames.
- **Hashes:** all 63 commit hashes resolve.

**Two things to note:**
- **A turn in both families:** turn-iNKHir is counted as both a go-ahead and a correction.
- **Turns not found:** 10 turns weren't found in their session's frames. I haven't looked at why yet.

**The next step** (job `invoke-1790738737288-28122-3e5f2574`, park `park-fe96ec23-ae31-433d-ab37-fca4e5c3f861`): the mission requires the baseline to be declared before measuring. It's committed, as `C2-baseline-declared.md` (581ce405), and codex-5 has to use it unchanged.
- **The claim tested:** a go-ahead is followed by a commit, or a park, more often than your other turns in the same sessions are.
- **Excluded:** "the agent replied" doesn't count, since that follows almost every turn.
- **The test itself:** leave-one-out, holding out each turn in turn.
- **Small families:** a family with fewer than 10 complete records is reported as too few to judge, which is where the correction family will land.

If the go-ahead rule beats the baseline, its record goes to claude-1 for the War Machine side.

Checking whether the rule's win survives a fairer baseline; one more computation.Gist: The first induced rule is in, and it beats the baseline as I declared it. But when I checked it against a fairer baseline, the evidence is only suggestive. The rule is for go-ahead turns: if the agent replied and committed in the previous turn, a go-ahead is followed by another commit. It predicted 16 of the 18 held-out turns where its condition held. That's weaker than it sounds, because the baseline I declared was too easy, which was my mistake. I've written down a stricter one before any further measurement. I didn't start another run; say if you want one.

**What I checked** (futon3c b86ca498):
- **Files:** only the intended ones.
- **Baseline:** unchanged from the one committed before the run.
- **Tests:** they rerun clean, and two planted bugs each fail a test:
  - fitting on all turns, with no holding out;
  - scoring a fact that's always true as better when it only ties.

**Why the result is weaker than it looks:**
- **Unmatched comparison:** my declared baseline compared go-ahead turns *where the rule's condition held* against *all* your other turns. But "the agent just committed" by itself makes another commit more likely. I also set no significance threshold.
- **Fairer comparison:** against your other turns *with the same condition*, the result is 16 of 18 against 124 of 181, or 89% against 69%. It still holds, but a one-sided test gives p ≈ 0.03 on only 18 turns. And the predicted fact (a commit) was picked from three candidates on the same data. So a go-ahead after a turn with commits is somewhat more often followed by a commit; that's suggestive, not established.
- **Correction family:** 7 complete records is too few to judge.

All of this is in the C2 note (8f1aebde), labelled as checked after the fact. The next test's declaration is written there too:
- the baseline is matched on the same condition;
- a result needs p < 0.05 after correcting for trying three candidate facts;
- the predicted fact is chosen inside each held-out fold.

**claude-1:** I've sent them the rule record's fields, which they need to design how the War Machine labels induced rules, together with this reading. I marked it "not for loading": the go-ahead move needs your turn to happen, and an unattended War Machine run has none, as claude-8 had already warned.

**Next:**
- **A War Machine rule** needs a correction family with more complete records. Most of the gaps are the 10 turns not found in the frames, which I haven't looked into yet.
- **Codex identity:** codex-4 is still working on giving Codex and Kimi processes their identity for signing.

Review mostly checks out; fixing one test that wrote fake agents' context files into the real directory.The 8 failures in that test predate codex-4's change: the same 8 fail at the commit before it. Committing the test fix, then extending `R` to cover dispatched work.Gist: Signing now covers every agent, and `R` covers dispatched work. Rewinding a turn also reverts commits made by any Codex or Kimi job that turn sent out, and leaves work dispatched by other sessions alone. codex-4's Agency change is reviewed and accepted, and the live tests show Codex and Kimi commits carrying all four lines. One gap: Claude seats already running, including me, only get the job and dispatcher lines after their next restart. Until then they still sign with their session.

**Review of codex-4's change** (4c269e12):
- **Files:** the three process launchers plus a small new namespace (`agent_context.clj`) that writes the job details. The job-start hook is in `http.clj`.
- **Stale-job case:** covered twice. A unit test checks that the second job's details replace the first's, and that a reader never sees a half-written file. Live, a second Codex job carried its own job id.
- **Non-agent processes:** the shell used by other peripherals only gets the agent variables when there's an agent.
- **Direct check:** I read `~/.futon/agent-context/codex-5.json` myself. It holds the second job's id, with me as caller and my session.
- **Tests:** codex-4 reported the targeted suites green and clean lint.

**One fix I made** (4929792f): an existing test suite (`job-timeout-test`) runs jobs for fake agents, so after this change it wrote four fake files into the real `~/.futon/agent-context`, the directory the hook reads. That suite now writes to a temporary directory. I removed the four files and confirmed nothing new lands there. The suite's 8 failures aren't from this change: the same 8 fail at the commit before it, which I ran in a scratch checkout.

**`R` with dispatched work** (f65d8b17, loaded):
- **The view:** a third label, `R (dispatched)`, for commits whose dispatcher is this session. A commit dispatched by another session stays `other seat`.
- **Tests:** 27 stepper tests pass. The test repo now has a commit dispatched by this session, which `R` reverts, and one dispatched by claude-9, which `R` leaves alone. Three tests fail on the old code.

**Other limits:**
- **codex-4's own commit** isn't signed: its process started before the change was loaded.
- **Repo list:** `R` only looks in repos named in the stepper's frames. Dispatched work in a repo the turn itself never touched isn't found yet.

Kimi-3's shell broke at 03:31, which is exactly when codex-4 reloaded `real_backend.clj` with new function arities. Checking for callers still using the old ones.Gist: kimi-3's scene driver is nearly finished, but its shell broke at 03:31, and the cause was codex-4's reload for commit signing. I've fixed it and sent kimi-3 back to finish. The reload changed how many arguments the shell function takes. Kimi's session was built before the reload, so it kept calling the old form, and every shell command failed. Any other Kimi or Zai seat was broken the same way from 03:31 until my fix went in (b4ba6c81), about six minutes later. The fix adds the old form back. It's reloaded, a live call succeeds, and all 25 backend tests pass.

**Where the scene driver stands** (from kimi-3's report; nothing committed yet):
- **Built:** the scene file with its steps (open buffer, type, press key, wait, assert, snapshot), the runner script, the recorded-answer stand-in agent, three scenes, and 5 unit tests. All pass the bracket check and compile cleanly.
- **Planted keymap bug:** that version of the scene failed at the `r` key, as it should.
- **Timeout:** the timeout scene reported "timed out" after 1 second, and the next scene still ran.
- **Not yet shown:** the fixed version passing. It was blocked by driver bugs kimi-3 fixed just before the shell broke.

**A change from the packet, which I've accepted:** kimi-3 found that playing keys back through Emacs's command loop can't work in a daemon with no frame. Typed text lands in `*scratch*`, and a space hangs the command loop. So the driver now looks up each key in the scene buffer's own keymaps and runs the bound command directly. That still fails on exactly the r/R keymap bug, which is what this test is for.

**Still open:** a key-lookup oddity kimi-3 saw inside a scene, which the rerun should confirm or explain.

**Next** (job `invoke-1790739437713-28136-049d449d`, park `park-1234f071-f52f-4b06-a6d0-261957ad0bf1`): kimi-3 reruns both acceptance tests, pastes the full report and commits. Then I run the runner myself once, including a check that it refuses any Emacs other than the test one, and close the task. I13 comes after that.

Gist: The scene driver is done and I've accepted it. I ran it myself: 4 scenes, all as expected. The fixed stepper passes, the planted keymap bug fails at the `r` key, and the timeout scene reports "timed out" while the next scene still runs. kimi-3 has already started on the next packet, I13: 象's trace rules checked on every new event, with any violation shown in 象's modeline indicator.

**What I checked:**
- **Commits:** futon4 19bc167f holds the driver, runner, three scenes, a fixture that reproduces the old bug, and 6 unit tests. futon3c 09ac3d95 holds one recorded agent answer. Nothing else was touched.
- **Refusal:** pointed at the ordinary Emacs server, the runner refuses with exit 2.
- **Expected failures:** a scene marked "expected to fail" only counts as passing if it really does fail, so the planted bug can't slip through as a pass.

**One small weakness:** the runner also has a guard on its own hard-coded server name, and that guard can never trip. The environment-variable check that does work is the one that matters, so I've left it.

**The space-key oddity is explained:** Emacs's key-description parser reads a single space as "no key", so the driver was looking up an empty key. Single characters now skip the parser, and there's a test for it. kimi-3 also saved notes on the three daemon pitfalls, for later packets that drive the REPL.

**Task E-kimi-task-135 is closed.**

**I13** (task E-kimi-task-136, job `invoke-1790739789958-28138-8e20694c`, park `park-d431c27a-d952-43a0-8ab8-9b4311294a24`). Three scenes accept it:
- a reply that ended without being sent to 象, older than 15 minutes, lights the modeline;
- the same thing when it's recent doesn't;
- once the turn is sent to 象 and ends in a failure, the light clears.

After reviewing it, I'll load it into your Emacs myself. I11 is next.

Planted bug now fails scene B, clean code passes. Committing that fix and loading I13 into your Emacs.Still getting the reaper test's stub right; one more look at why it fails.Gist: I13 is accepted and live in your Emacs: 象's rules now run on every new event, and a violation shows in 象's modeline. Turning it on exposed two real problems, both now fixed:
- **The test daemon was testing stale code.** It stayed up between runs, and `require` never reloads, so a planted bug still passed.
- **The reaper gave up too early.** It stopped checking on 象 after 9 minutes. With 象 backed up tonight, 18 readings landed later than that, so the stepper never reloaded for them and the new check would have shown them as never read.

**I13 review** (futon3c 881ddb78, futon4 7d52d16, task E-kimi-task-136 closed):
- **Checks on every event:** the rules re-run over the last 200 events whenever one is recorded.
- **The indicator:** a violation adds `!reply end → dispatch ×N` next to 象's modeline indicator, and clicking it opens the check buffer. 象's existing health states are unchanged.
- **Can't break recording:** an error inside the check never stops recording.
- **The run:** all 7 scenes pass.

**Fix 1: the stale test daemon** (futon4 47ded9d). With the rule's 15-minute grace period removed, every I13 scene still passed. The cause was the long-running daemon. The runner now starts a fresh daemon every run. With that fix, the planted bug fails scene B and clean code passes 7 of 7.

**Fix 2: the reaper** (futon3c d7ff8079, loaded). It now checks at 3, 6 and 9 minutes, then every 10 minutes for up to an hour. It also treats "queued" as unfinished; before, a queued job was never checked again. Two new tests cover a late landing and the one-hour stop; both fail on the old code. I also recorded the 18 missed landings once by hand. That leaves no violations, just 4 recent turns still waiting on 象.

**Signing gap:** kimi-3's commits aren't signed yet. Its session was built before codex-4's change was loaded, so it passes no identity. It will sign after its next restart.

**Next:** I11, the "as of this frame" view in the stepper, goes to kimi-3 when you want it. I'm holding it for now because 象 has a backlog.
